denials.summary: Confirmed buying from Kanzamin but denied the coltan came from Rubaya; says it disengaged from Kanzamin pending stronger due diligence, and that GW showed no transaction-level proof.
Denied any contractual or commercial relationship with Boss Mining Solution.
Denied having received coltan from African Panther Resources.
Denied buying any Rubaya material in 2023, citing geo-fingerprinting.
Strongly denied that the Kotecha family profited from conflict minerals and denied sourcing conflict minerals from Rubaya; said Ketankumar Kotecha is a stakeholder, not operationally involved.
Said a Kigali visit found no anomalies in Boss Mining Solution's export volumes and that shipments originated in Rwanda and met ITSCI requirements.
Previously denied sourcing conflict coltan, citing due diligence; did not reply to GW's later letter.
Strongly denied that coltan from African Panther, Rani or Hillside was from DRC or conflict-linked; cites mineralogy and mine-level tracing; says it stopped sourcing Rwandan tantalum in May 2025.
Denied sourcing conflict material from DRC and denied any connection to Chris Huber.
Denied being or ever having been a beneficial owner or member of Tawotin.
Denied trading conflict minerals from Rubaya and denied any connection to John Crawley.
Said it found no sign of smuggled or conflict minerals at East Group Minerals, citing ITSCI membership; director Ignas Pilvinis said Andrius Jankunas was never a Minterra director.
Former Minterra CEO said only documented material was bought in his time and that he has no relationship with Darius Krasauskas beyond the surname.
